To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) adversarial machine learning defense techniques are less effective against a machine learning classifier that can be trained with adversarial samples, and (2) enforcing statistical privacy guarantees is an effective way to protect streaming traffic privacy from machine learning based traffic analysis.

(1) Adversarial samples can be used to confound the traffic classifier, but the adversary can adapt by changing the classifier; and (2) Differential privacy is effective against statistical inference based analysis of encrypted streaming traffic, while remaining agnostics to the machine learning classifier used by the adversary.

(i) the effectiveness of adversarial samples is limited when the adversary can change the classifier, but (ii) differential privacy is very effective against statistical inference based traffic classification, and (iii) our empirical evaluation suggests that our proposed mechanisms for differential privacy for encrypted traffic are promising solutions in this scenario.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the privacy implications of machine learning powered traffic analysis, and the effectiveness and limitations of existing techniques in mitigating the threat.

the following questions. Can we use adversarial machine learning to protect the traffic privacy in streaming applications? What are the limitations of this approach? Can we achieve differential privacy guarantees for streaming applications? What is the cost of enforcing such guarantees?

the following questions: 1) How to defend against machine learning based analysis of streaming encrypted traffic? 2) How to enforce privacy for streaming encrypted traffic? We provide answers to these questions by proposing and evaluating the effectiveness of two defense mechanisms: adversarial training and differential privacy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
differential privacy is a promising solution for the problem of traffic analysis, while adversarial machine learning is not.

the proposed differential privacy approaches provide a strong defense against statistical inference based traffic analyses, while being less effective against attacks based on machine learning classifiers that can adapt to the defenses.
the statistical privacy approaches are more effective than the adversarial samples based approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
statistical privacy guarantees are effective against statistical inference based traffic analyses, and can be used to protect the privacy of streaming traffic.
differential privacy can be a promising defense against machine learning powered traffic analysis attacks.
statistical privacy guarantees are very promising in the context of encrypted streaming traffic, while adversarial samples are not as effective as expected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
differential privacy provides an effective defense against statistical inference attacks, and is a promising approach to protect users' privacy in encrypted streaming traffic.
the statistical properties of streaming traffic can be used for privacy protection, even in the context of machine learning based traffic analysis.
the statistical privacy techniques, which are well studied in the context of differential privacy, are effective in mitigating machine learning powered traffic analysis attacks.
